history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The lead's decisions on the engine (the seven FINDINGS defaults accepted; Adan and Resing and Iversen cited for figures and formulas and never quoted; the Table 5.1 c = 5 figure taught as a printed slip; the Skoko PSV total left out because the rounded days do not reproduce it) landed before any lesson was written; that is provenance.

cleared_claims: The three rows differ only in what the weather input states, so a plan names both the factor and the activities.

The first three rows are three voyages of demand, whatever the double arithmetic leaves in the last digit; the fourth asks for a thousandth of a square metre more than three voyages carry, and rounds up to four.
cleared_claims_note: Read by hand 2026-09-27: Section 9 prints exactly three rows (calm, the fixture factor on sailing and field, the factor on every activity) and they differ only in the weather input; Section 15's first three rows each return 3 voyages (engine) and the fourth 4.
sourceRule: Every source is named with its edition or date, its licence and the date read (2026-09-27), printed in digest section 2; quote_check.py pins every file's sha256 prefix, cross-checks the six prefixes FINDINGS-marine.md records, and checks every figure the digest cites in its text. The course quotes NO source prose: Adan and Resing (lecture notes, 26 March 2015) and Iversen (ITU-D draft, 20 June 2001) print no licence, so their figures and formulas are cited and their prose never quoted (the lead's decision); the Wikipedia article (revision 1317275412) is CC BY-SA 4.0, cited and never pasted; Aas, Halskau and Wallace (2009) is publisher copyright, by concept only; Skoko et al. (2024) and the arXiv paper 2102.05851v2 are CC BY 4.0 and cited by table and equation. gate_no_source_prose.py refuses any eight-word run of the six texts in anything a learner reads (a run of eight numbers is a list of figures, and the three source titles are citations). Two printed slips are taught as slips: Adan and Resing Table 5.1 prints 1.53 at c = 5 where the formula gives 1.524986; Skoko et al.'s PSV total (USD 186,274.10) is not reproduced by their rounded Table 5 days (186214.104 through the engine), so the course uses the AHTS row.

openReadings.capacity: a load exactly at a capacity is feasible (inclusive at twelve significant digits). Never graded: bit-identical under reading_capacity_exclusive.
openReadings.binding tie: a tie of utilisations goes to the first constraint in the order deck area, deck load, deadweight, tanks. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_binding_tie_last.
openReadings.rounding key: a count rounds up on its twelve-digit figure. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_ceil_without_key.
openReadings.nearest halves: the nearest whole vessel rounds a half up. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_nearest_halves_down.
openReadings.demand and minimum visits: demand equal to the minimum visits names the demand. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_tie_names_minimum_visits.
openReadings.FFD ties: first-fit decreasing puts the heavier of two equal footprints first. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_ffd_tie_lighter_first.
openReadings.deck fit: a unit that fills the deck exactly fits. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_deck_fit_exclusive.
openReadings.berth target: a target is met at or below it. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_berth_target_strict.
openReadings.short: short means strictly above the planned capacity. Never graded: bit-identical under reading_short_at_equality (no graded field is a Monte Carlo figure).
openReadings.P90 of a requirement: the low figure (the 10th percentile). Never graded: bit-identical under reading_p90_high, and on a second seed and draw count.

statedChoices: The activities the weather slows, the voyage and vessel rounding rules, the packing rule, the queue model and the concurrent choice are INPUTS, not readings: every capstone states each one it uses, marine_capstone.mjs records per field whether the other option moves it (19 field-choice pairs move past the tolerance and are stated in the case, 23 are bit-identical), and discriminate.mjs aims the other option at each field it moves as a wrong term.

scopeSeams.the cash flow ledger, discounting and NP: OWNED BY the cashflow course; this course discounts nothing.

namingCollisions.voyage: one sailing from the base and back; a milk run is one voyage through every stop.
namingCollisions.binding: the constraint with the highest utilisation, by the stated tie rule.
namingCollisions.vessel-days: voyages times voyage days, added over the sets.
namingCollisions.wait: the mean wait in the queue on the working-hour clock.
namingCollisions.P90: of a requirement or a cost, the LOW figure, quoted with its seed and draws.

openItems.ENGINE FINDINGS: Two optional findings for a repair-first engines PR, neither blocking the foundation: (1) wording, the third deckPlan overflow reason ("no voyage has X m2 of usable area and Y t of deck load left") does not say which of the two limits is exhausted, so on the Ekene one-voyage deck it reads as though deck load were short when only area is; (2) coverage, deckPlan.lowerBound counts the area and weight of units no voyage can ever carry (a footprint above the usable deck or a weight above the deck load), so on deck-item-larger-than-deck the bound is 3 for cargo whose carriable part fits one voyage. The course teaches both exactly as the engine returns them.
